result:
Both integrate one branch's changes into another; difference is history shape.

`git merge feature`: creates merge commit with two parents, joins histories as they happened. Existing commits untouched → safe on shared branches. Cost: non-linear graph, noisy with many merges. Conflicts resolved once.

`git rebase main`: replays your commits on top of `main` as new commits (new SHAs) → linear history, no merge commit. Cost: rewrites history. Rebasing commits others already pulled → their history diverges, needs `git push --force-with-lease`. Conflicts may recur per replayed commit.

Rule: rebase local/unpushed work to tidy it up, merge for shared/public branches. Never rebase a branch others build on.
